text: Docker is a platform that allows developers to package applications and their dependencies into containers. Containers ensure consistency across environments and are lightweight compared to virtual machines.
A Docker image is a read-only template used to create containers. A container is a running instance of an image and can be started, stopped, and deleted.
A Dockerfile is a script that contains instructions to build a Docker image. Each instruction creates a layer, and Docker caches layers to optimize build speed.
The docker build command creates an image from a Dockerfile. It uses a build context and supports tagging images using the -t flag.
The docker run command creates and starts a container from an image. Common options include -d for detached mode and -p for port mapping.
Port mapping in Docker allows exposing container ports to the host system. The syntax is -p host_port:container_port.
Docker volumes are used to persist data outside of containers. They are managed by Docker and provide better performance and portability than bind mounts.
Docker Compose is a tool used to define and run multi-container applications using a YAML configuration file.
Docker networks enable communication between containers. The default network types include bridge, host, and none.
Docker layer caching speeds up image builds by reusing unchanged layers. Proper ordering of Dockerfile instructions improves caching efficiency.
The FROM instruction in a Dockerfile specifies the base image. It is usually the first instruction and defines the starting point of the build.
The WORKDIR instruction sets the working directory inside the container. All subsequent commands run relative to this directory.
The COPY instruction copies files from the host system into the container image during the build process.
The RUN instruction executes commands during image build time, such as installing packages or dependencies.
The CMD instruction defines the default command that runs when a container starts. It can be overridden at runtime.
The docker ps command lists running containers. Using -a shows all containers including stopped ones.
The docker stop command stops a running container gracefully, allowing processes to terminate properly.
The docker rm command removes a container from the system. The container must be stopped before removal.
The docker images command lists all locally available Docker images on the system.
The docker logs command retrieves logs from a container, which is useful for debugging and monitoring application behavior.
